title: Segal presheaves and coefficient localization
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], coherent functors, mapping spaces, homotopy fibers, full subcategories and (co)limits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], monoidal infinity categories from [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], and cartesian and cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Presheaves and their Yoneda embedding have the meaning of [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density]; their small colimits exist by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] and are computed pointwise as in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. A left Kan extension of $F$ along $u$ means a functor $u_!F$ with a unit $F\to u^*u_!F$ inducing, naturally in $G$, an equivalence of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}(u_!F,G)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(F,u^*G)$. For a small monoidal infinity category $C$, put $P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Spc})$. Day convolution on $P(C)$ is left Kan extension of the external cartesian product of presheaves along the opposite of the tensor functor $C\times C\to C$. Write $C_\otimes\to\Delta$ for the cartesian fibration classified by the same functor $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ as $C^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, using [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] and its opposite; its fibre at $[n]$ is equivalent to $C^n$. Write $[n](c_1,\ldots,c_n)$ for its objects, $\Delta^n(\boldsymbol c)$ for their represented presheaves on $C_\otimes$, and $v=\Delta^0$ for the vertex representable. For a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, cartesian transport sends $\boldsymbol c$ to the list with $j$th entry $\bigotimes_{\alpha(j-1)<i\leq\alpha(j)}c_i$, with an empty tensor equal to the monoidal unit. The cartesian arrows over the consecutive inclusions $[1]\to[n]$, $0\mapsto i-1$, $1\mapsto i$, and over the vertex inclusions $[0]\to[n]$ give the edge and vertex maps of representables. The labelled spine is $\Delta^1(c_1)\amalg_v\cdots\amalg_v\Delta^1(c_n)$, gluing the target of edge $i$ to the source of edge $i+1$, with its induced map to $\Delta^n(\boldsymbol c)$. All fiber products in the Segal condition below are homotopy fiber products, using these source and target maps. A Segal presheaf is $Z\in P(C_\otimes)$ for which
$$Z([n](\boldsymbol c))\longrightarrow Z([1](c_1))\times_{Z([0])}\cdots\times_{Z([0])}Z([1](c_n))$$
is an equivalence for every $n\geq2$ and every list $\boldsymbol c$. Their full subcategory is $Q_C$.

For $\phi\in P(C)$ let $J_C(\phi)$ be left Kan extension along the fibre inclusion $C^{\mathrm{op}}=(C_\otimes^{\mathrm{op}})_{[1]}\hookrightarrow C_\otimes^{\mathrm{op}}$, and let $a_\phi=\operatorname{colim}_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}\phi$. For a space $a$ and presheaf $F$, the copower $a\cdot F$ has values $a\times F(-)$. Define the free edge with two specified endpoints by the presheaf pushout
$$E_C(\phi)=J_C(\phi)\amalg_{a_\phi\cdot(v\amalg v)}(v\amalg v).$$
The two maps $v\to\Delta^1(c)$, natural in $c$, give the first leg of this pushout after the Yoneda colimit expression of $\phi$; the second leg forgets $a_\phi$. Equivalently this is the colimit of the represented edges $\Delta^1(c)$ indexed by the category of elements of $\phi$ (the total right fibration over $C$ classified by $\phi$ in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]), taken in the category of presheaves under $v\amalg v$. In particular $E_C(\varnothing)=v\amalg v$.

For a small set $S$ of arrows of $P(C)$, let $P^S(C)$ be the full subcategory of $S$-local objects: $M$ is local if $\operatorname{Map}(\psi,M)\to\operatorname{Map}(\phi,M)$ is an equivalence for each $(\phi\to\psi)\in S$. An $S$-local equivalence is an arrow $f:A\to B$ for which $\operatorname{Map}(B,M)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,M)$ is an equivalence for every $S$-local $M$. Call $S$ monoidally compatible if tensoring any arrow of $S$ on either side with any presheaf is an $S$-local equivalence (equivalently, is inverted by the reflector when that reflector exists). Let $Q_C^S\subset Q_C$ consist of the Segal presheaves local for all arrows $E_C(\phi)\to E_C(\psi)$ induced by $S$. For $Z\in Q_C$ and $(x,y)\in Z([0])^2$, write
$$H_Z(x,y)(c)=\operatorname{fib}_{(x,y)}\bigl(Z([1](c))\longrightarrow Z([0])^2\bigr)$$
for its mapping presheaf. A reflector onto a full subcategory $i:Q\hookrightarrow P$ means a functor $L:P\to Q$ with a unit $\mathrm{id}_P\to iL$ inducing natural mapping-space equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_Q(LA,M)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_P(A,iM)$. A Segal equivalence is a map inverted by reflection into $Q_C$; an $S$-local Segal equivalence is a map in $Q_C$ inverted by reflection into $Q_C^S$. Denote these reflectors, when they exist, by $L_C$ and $L_C^S$; denote inclusions by $i_C$ and $i_C^S$, respectively.

For small monoidal $C,D$, $X\in P(C_\otimes)$ and $Y\in P(D_\otimes)$, define $X\boxtimes Y\in P((C\times D)_\otimes)$ by restriction of the external product along $(C\times D)_\otimes\simeq C_\otimes\times_\Delta D_\otimes\to C_\otimes\times D_\otimes$, namely
$$(X\boxtimes Y)([n](\boldsymbol c,\boldsymbol d))=X([n](\boldsymbol c))\times Y([n](\boldsymbol d)).$$
For monoidally compatible small sets $S$ in $P(C)$ and $T$ in $P(D)$, define the set of arrows in $P(C\times D)$ by the union $$S\odot T=\{s\boxtimes\mathrm{id}_{y_D(d)}:s\in S,\ d\in D\}\ \cup\ \{\mathrm{id}_{y_C(c)}\boxtimes t:c\in C,\ t\in T\},$$ where $y_C,y_D$ are Yoneda and this external product is the product of presheaf values. Its domain distinguishes this notation from the operadic algebroid external product.
